subfields.name: Foundations & Exact Resampling
subfields.summary: Unbiased walker splitting and merging, probability conservation, resampling variance, and ergodic theory descending from Huber and Kim 1996.

questions.q: Does adaptive or time dependent bin updating bias transient or stationary Weighted Ensemble path expectations?
questions.detail: Path space resampling derivations (Zhang, Jasnow & Zuckerman 2010) and discrete time selection mutation martingale theorems (Aristoff 2018, Aristoff 2022) establish zero estimator bias for finite horizon expectations and almost sure ergodic convergence for time averages across arbitrary history dependent or adaptive Voronoi partitions whenever resampling conserves conditional walker weights and daughter trajectories evolve under independent stochastic transitions.

questions.q: Does uniform walker allocation per bin guarantee lower variance than brute force Monte Carlo simulation?
questions.detail: Exact finite population variance formulas (Aristoff 2022) and asymptotic Central Limit Theorem bounds (Webber, Aristoff & Simpson 2020) prove that equal walker counts per bin along poorly aligned coordinates can produce larger variance than brute force Monte Carlo, whereas allocating walkers proportional to bin weight times intrabin Poisson discrepancy standard deviation approaches the sharp mu(v_f)^2 / N variance floor.

questions.q: How can post simulation kinetic estimators aggregate multi lag Weighted Ensemble trajectories without coarse state discretization or trajectory merging bias?
questions.detail: Coarse Markov transition matrices built at lags exceeding the Weighted Ensemble resampling step suffer trajectory merging bias when pruned weights merge onto distinct microstates (Bose, Kilinc & Dickson 2025), while equilibrium weighted coarse matrices fail on directional steady states whenever intrabin relaxation lags behind bin exit (Aristoff, Webber & Zuckerman 2026).

subfields.name: Steady State, Hill Flux & Non Markovian Rates
subfields.summary: Hill steady state relation, history labeled ensembles, event duration estimators (RED), first passage times, and discretization free reweighting (RiteWeight).

questions.q: Under what boundary condition does inverse steady state target flux reproduce the exact equilibrium mean reaction time?
questions.detail: For any return process reinjected on reactant boundary A according to probability measure pi, inverse stationary sink flux matches the mean hitting time initiated from pi. Recovering the equilibrium mean reaction time T_AB requires reinjection matching the reactive boundary entry distribution nu_E on boundary A rather than a Boltzmann slice or fixed point source (Baudel, Guyader and Lelievre 2023).

questions.q: When should pre steady state Weighted Ensemble rate estimation prefer RED event duration scaling, haMSM microbins, or RiteWeight segment reweighting?
questions.detail: RED removes short trajectory ramp bias without spatial clustering once barrier crossings reach the sink (DeGrave, Bogetti and Chong 2021), microbin haMSMs extrapolate steady state flux across thousands of history labeled states (Copperman and Zuckerman 2020), and RiteWeight eliminates fixed cluster discretization error via randomized hyperplanes (Kania et al. 2026), with finite sample variance tradeoffs under active comparison.

questions.q: How should steady state flux uncertainty and truncation windows be calibrated under genealogical walker correlations and extreme weight skew?
questions.detail: Walker splitting creates shared trajectory ancestry while rare event weights span more than 100 orders of magnitude. Integrating MSER 5 startup truncation (White, Cobb and Spratt 2002) and lugsail lag window covariance corrections (Vats and Flegal 2021) with ancestral tree correlation estimators remains an open statistical challenge.

subfields.name: Adaptive Binning & Allocation
subfields.summary: Minimal Adaptive Binning (MAB), WExplore Voronoi hierarchies, REVO variation optimization, string bins, and discrepancy driven walker allocation.

questions.q: Does dynamic on the fly bin boundary adjustment introduce statistical bias into Weighted Ensemble kinetic estimators?
questions.detail: Path space resampling proofs establish that statistical weights attach to individual trajectories rather than spatial bins. When splitting divides parent weight w_i evenly across child replicas and pruning selects survivors proportional to w_i while summing merged weights, adaptive Voronoi strings, Minimal Adaptive Binning boundaries, and binless resamplers preserve exact non equilibrium expectations at every resampling interval tau.

questions.q: Why does uniform walker allocation per rectilinear bin underperform discrepancy weighted allocation?
questions.detail: Uniform walker targets across M^d hyperrectangular grids expend trajectories in unoccupied or flat committor off pathway basins. Asymptotic martingale variance theory proves that scaling walker counts with bin weight times one step flux discrepancy standard deviation w_i sigma_i, or continuous steady state density pi(x) v(x), minimizes flux variance and prevents cases where naive geometric bins exceed brute force variance.

questions.q: Do regionless variation optimization resamplers surpass adaptive Voronoi and rectilinear partitions for quantitative binding free energies and multi lag Markov models?
questions.detail: Regionless variation optimization in REVO removes hard Voronoi cell walls in high dimensional spaces, whereas unconstrained pairwise distance maximization over clones quasi unbound ligand poses into tiny weight exits and introduces trajectory merging bias into Markov state models at lag intervals tau exceeding the Weighted Ensemble resampling step tau_0 unless paired with quasi unbound cloning cutoffs or merging bias corrected transition estimators.

subfields.name: History Augmented MSMs & Koopman Models
subfields.summary: History augmented Markov state models (haMSM), transition path theory, microbinning, spectral Koopman analysis, and stationary distribution estimation.

questions.q: Do variationally validated reversible Markov state models reproduce first passage times at nanosecond lag times?
questions.detail: No. Across Chignolin, Trp cage, Villin, and NTL9 folding benchmarks, implied timescale validation guarantees slow correlation decay without removing non Markovian recrossing bias below 100 ns lag times, whereas unsymmetrized history augmented Markov state models recover unbiased mean first passage times at the frame interval.

questions.q: Should stationary reweighting and committor estimation rely on discrete microbin transition matrices or basis set Koopman operators?
questions.detail: Fine k means microbinning on transient Weighted Ensemble data exhibits high variance across sparse barrier clusters unless cross validated across odd and even iteration blocks, motivating randomized tessellation averaging, Galerkin spectral stratification in BAD NEUS, and neural semigroup committor solvers in WELP.

questions.q: Can variance optimal discrepancy and local variation coordinates be learned online for underdamped atomistic proteins?
questions.detail: Asymptotic Weighted Ensemble variance bounds prove optimal walker allocation scales with stationary density times local flux variation on discrepancy rectangles, cutting high friction folding flux spread by more than twenty orders of magnitude while low friction inertial regimes still exhibit run to run instability.

subfields.name: Software, GPU Engines & Workflows
subfields.summary: WESTPA 1.0 and 2.0, wepy, OpenMM GPU acceleration, trajectory storage schemas, pathway analysis packages (lpath), and synthetic dynamics benchmarks.

questions.q: Do consolidated HDF5 trajectory containers eliminate filesystem bottlenecks without slowing GPU Weighted Ensemble throughput?
questions.detail: Yes. Per iteration HDF5 walker archives in WESTPA 2.0 and lineage indexed WepyHDF5 stores in wepy remove million file metadata contention across multi GPU clusters while shrinking trajectory footprints by 27 to 85 percent with negligible runtime overhead.

questions.q: Does text string sequence alignment of discretized walker trajectories produce partition invariant pathway classes?
questions.detail: LPATH groups reactive trajectories efficiently after two stage clustering and consecutive repeat condensation, whereas shared ancestor segments in Weighted Ensemble splitting trees and non consecutive barrier recrossings shift route fractions relative to frame medoid and fundamental sequence metrics.

questions.q: How should Weighted Ensemble toolkits validate machine learned potentials and automate steady state haMSM restarts?
questions.detail: Modular WESTPA propagators now evaluate neural force fields across multi protein TICA benchmarks, while automated haMSM restart workflows still depend on empirical post restart burn in cutoffs and odd even block cross validation to guard against sparse microbin instabilities.

subfields.name: Ligand Binding, Unbinding & Residence Time
subfields.summary: Small molecule association and dissociation kinetics, drug residence times, trypsin benzamidine, host guest cavities, BRD4, and HSP90 inhibitors.

questions.q: Can unbiased Weighted Ensemble trajectories recover drug residence times on the seconds-to-minutes timescale without biasing forces?
questions.detail: Hierarchical Voronoi WExplore and regionless REVO protocols sample continuous unbinding path ensembles for soluble epoxide hydrolase inhibitors and TSPO ligands with residence times spanning tens of seconds to hundreds of minutes from microsecond aggregate trajectories, typically within one order of magnitude of experimental measurements.

questions.q: Do rate-ratio binding free energies from Weighted Ensemble match alchemical benchmarks on identical force fields?
questions.detail: Raw k_off over k_on ratios in SAMPL6 deviated from alchemical benchmarks by 3 to 5 kcal/mol until analytical finite-box volume, state-boundary, and screened unbound electrostatic corrections plus Cutoff-REVO walker management reduced discrepancies below 1 kcal/mol, though alchemical perturbation remains roughly tenfold cheaper for affinity alone.

questions.q: Why do atomistic force fields mispredict dissociation rates by up to four orders of magnitude for interior protein cavities?
questions.detail: In internal-cavity HIF-2alpha PAS-B ligand escape under ff19SB and GAFF2, steady-state Minimal Adaptive Binning Weighted Ensemble identified the experimentally validated N288 gate while overestimating k_off by four orders of magnitude against ZZ-exchange NMR, implicating missing electronic polarization, cavity hydration energetics, and slow protein reorganization.

subfields.name: Protein Association & Brownian Dynamics
subfields.summary: Diffusion controlled bimolecular encounter, barnase barstar association, electrostatic steering, Northrup Allison McCammon surfaces, and multiscale BD MD schemes.

questions.q: Can explicit-solvent atomistic Weighted Ensemble reproduce experimental diffusion-influenced protein-protein association rate constants?
questions.detail: Equilibrium Weighted Ensemble on barnase and barstar in explicit TIP3P water generated 203 continuous atomistic binding pathways in 18 microseconds and produced k_on = (2.3 +- 1.0) x 10^8 M^-1 s^-1 against experimental (2.86 +- 0.7) x 10^8 M^-1 s^-1, with Rate from Event Durations (RED) cutting required trajectory cost by over 25 percent.

questions.q: Does helical preorganization accelerate association of intrinsically disordered peptides with globular protein partners?
questions.detail: Controlled Brownian dynamics Weighted Ensemble comparisons of disordered p53 peptide and four exact preorganized analogues binding MDM2 with hydrodynamic interactions produced k_on = (5.7 +- 0.6) x 10^7 M^-1 s^-1 versus (5.1 +- 0.8) x 10^7 M^-1 s^-1, demonstrating identical association kinetics within statistical uncertainty.

questions.q: To what extent does accidental cancellation between low water-model viscosity and periodic hydrodynamic drag mask transport errors in explicit-solvent k_on?
questions.detail: TIP3P underestimates experimental water shear viscosity by roughly 2.5-fold while finite periodic boxes impose Yeh-Hummer Oseen drag proportional to 1/L, and four-point OPC water still requires temperature-dependent viscosity corrections ranging from 10 percent at 298 K to 20 percent at 273 K.

subfields.name: Protein Folding & Disordered Ensembles
subfields.summary: Atomistic folding pathways and rates across chignolin, trp cage, villin, NTL9, calbindin, p53 peptides, and intrinsically disordered proteins.

questions.q: Can history-augmented Markov state models eliminate the lag-time bias of standard Markov state models on atomistic protein folding?
questions.detail: Across >100 microsecond Anton trajectories of chignolin, Trp-cage, villin, and NTL9, standard Markov state models underestimate folding mean first-passage times by an order of magnitude or more unless lag times exceed ~100 ns, whereas history-augmented Markov models and RiteWeight recover exact reference folding times at sub-nanosecond lags.

questions.q: Why do independent Weighted Ensemble protein folding replicates exhibit flux variance spanning tens of orders of magnitude?
questions.detail: Heavy-tailed log-variance across 13 to 20 independent NTL9 and Protein G runs (spanning 20 to 70 orders of magnitude) arises from orthogonal slow intermediates and suboptimal RMSD progress coordinates, causing standard and Bayesian bootstrap intervals to undercover the true mean until discrepancy-variance bin optimization narrows spread by over 20 orders.

questions.q: Do current generative artificial-intelligence ensemble predictors sample true Boltzmann distributions for flexible or mutated proteins?
questions.detail: Side-by-side benchmarking of BioEmu, AFSample2, and ESMFlow uncovers mutually inconsistent conformational distributions and muted responses to state-shifting point mutations, requiring physics-based Weighted Ensemble relaxation plus RiteWeight reweighting to erase starting-ensemble bias.

subfields.name: Large Assemblies, Viral Spikes & Allostery
subfields.summary: Multimillion atom viral glycoproteins, coronaviral spike glycan gating, calmodulin, adenylate kinase, GPCR activation, and large conformational switches.

questions.q: Can atomistic Weighted Ensemble sample continuous seconds-timescale conformational activation in half-million-atom glycosylated viral spikes?
questions.detail: Equilibrium and AI-coupled Weighted Ensemble simulations on 100 to 192 GPUs generated 310 wild-type and over 800 Delta SARS-CoV-2 spike RBD opening pathways in explicit solvent, discovering the experimental N343 glycan gate and D614-K854 salt-bridge allosteric switch.

questions.q: Do equilibrium Weighted Ensemble viral spike simulations furnish converged macroscopic opening rate constants k_open?
questions.detail: No. Tens of nanoseconds of unrecycled molecular time remain in the transient pre-steady-state regime, requiring terabyte-scale history-augmented Markov model postprocessing to estimate macroscopic k_open, whereas mean pathway sampling times act strictly like relative kinetic readiness metrics across variants.

questions.q: Can Weighted Ensemble bridge all-atom modulator binding to complete icosahedral viral capsid self-assembly?
questions.detail: Tabulated coarse-grained Monte Carlo Weighted Ensemble reached complete 120-dimer Hepatitis B virus capsids from 110-dimer intermediates and all-atom Weighted Ensemble resolved AT-130 and GLS4 modulator shifts in early tetramers, while full atomistic assembly kinetics from free dimers remain open.

subfields.name: Membranes, Permeation & Channels
subfields.summary: Passive membrane permeability, lipid bilayer partitioning, ion channels, membrane transporters, and pore gating rare events.

questions.q: Does steady-state Weighted Ensemble flux overcome the 1D Markovian assumption of inhomogeneous solubility-diffusion for drug membrane permeability?
questions.detail: Steady-state Minimal Adaptive Binning plus WESS reweighting computes P_m = k_DA l_D from continuous all-atom POPC crossing trajectories without assuming memoryless 1D z-diffusion, matching MDCK-LE and PAMPA log P_m within ~0.4 to 1.1 log units across tacrine, sotalol, and (R)-zacopride in 6 to 8 microseconds per compound.

questions.q: Do lipophilic membrane-protein ligands dissociate into aqueous bulk or laterally through the lipid bilayer?
questions.detail: Over 40 microseconds of REVO and Markov modeling on translocator protein TSPO with neuroimaging ligand PK-11195 captured 2285 exit events exclusively through inter-helical fenestrations into the lipid membrane, with the rate-limiting transition state occurring after protein separation inside the bilayer.

questions.q: How strongly do fixed protonation states, nonpolarizable lipids, and z-bin widths bias permeation rates of charged or ionizable solutes?
questions.detail: Coarse 0.25 A z-bins stalled Arg9 translocation inside the hydrophobic core until refinement to 0.10 A bins uncovered water-defect and lipid co-transport pathways, while continuous constant-pH Weighted Ensemble on fentanyl demonstrated that dynamic deprotonation shifts permeation kinetics omitted by fixed-charge topologies.

subfields.name: Collective Variables & Deep Learning
subfields.summary: Information bottleneck (SPIB), variational autoencoders, unsupervised progress coordinates, AlphaFold seeded ensembles, and rotational alignment metrics.

questions.q: Does unconstrained orthogonal SVD coordinate alignment produce a physically valid macromolecular RMSD collective variable?
questions.detail: Minimizing coordinate residuals over the full orthogonal group O(3) in Kabsch 1976 admits improper inversions with det(U) = -1 whenever cross covariance determinant det(X Y^T) turns negative, flipping chiral L residues into D enantiomers. Restricting alignment to proper special orthogonal rotations via the third singular vector sign factor d = det(W V^T) in Kabsch 1978, or maximizing the traceless symmetric 4x4 quaternion form alongside graph automorphism permutation for symmetric ligands, is mandatory for exact rigid body RMSD evaluation.

questions.q: Does elevated AlphaFold2 pLDDT or AlphaFold3 secondary structure prove constitutive folding of an isolated protein region?
questions.detail: AlphaFold2 assigns high confidence (pLDDT >= 70) to conditionally folded intrinsically disordered regions stabilized by binding partners or post translational modifications despite disorder in apo solution, and AlphaFold3 diffusion networks hallucinate spurious helices inside disordered tails unless curbed by cross distillation. Static or MSA subsampled AI predictions lack Boltzmann probabilities and require physics based trajectory reweighting.

questions.q: Can online unsupervised deep collective variables discover unvisited reaction channels without human progress coordinates?
questions.detail: Variational autoencoders and State Predictive Information Bottleneck encoders trained on ongoing Weighted Ensemble segments compress transitions among visited basins while collapsing unsampled barriers, requiring hybrid expert coordinates, latent outlier scoring, or stopped process committor semigroup losses to drive exploration into unvisited regions without inflating replicate rate variance.

subfields.name: Statistical Estimators & Sibling Rare Event Methods
subfields.summary: Milestoning, forward flux sampling, adaptive multilevel splitting, block bootstrap, Kish effective sample size, and correlated uncertainty quantification.

questions.q: Why do standard error bars and ordinary nonparametric bootstrap intervals fail on small sample Weighted Ensemble rate replicates?
questions.detail: Across 10 to 15 independent atomistic Weighted Ensemble runs whose flux estimates span multiple orders of magnitude (log 10 standard deviation above 1), normal standard error intervals extend to unphysical negative rates and Efron nonparametric bootstrap systematically biases lower log space confidence bounds downward whenever resamples omit rare high weight arrivals (Mostofian & Zuckerman 2019).

questions.q: Can Dirichlet Bayesian bootstrap or dependent block bootstrap achieve nominal 95 percent mean rate coverage without parametric tail assumptions?
questions.detail: Dirichlet weighted Bayesian bootstrap eliminates the artificial lower bound cliff of standard multinomial bootstrap on skewed replicates, whereas both bootstrap variants still undercover the true arithmetic mean in roughly 30 percent of heavy tailed synthetic benchmarks (Mostofian & Zuckerman 2019), and time series block bootstrap requires distinct block size exponents n^(1/3), n^(1/4), and n^(1/5) for variance versus one sided and two sided intervals (Hall, Horowitz & Jing 1995).

questions.q: How should Weighted Ensemble Milestoning equilibrate high dimensional milestone hypersurfaces without harmonic restraint overhead?
questions.detail: Weighted Ensemble Milestoning accelerates inter milestone transitions (Ray & Andricioaei 2020), while launching runs from single milestone structures undersamples orthogonal slow modes on protein ligand interfaces (Ray, Gokey, Mobley & Andricioaei 2020), motivating exact milestoning hitting distribution iteration without harmonic bias artifacts.
